author: The Epistle to Diognetus
note: The famous 'sweet exchange' of this anonymous 2nd-century apology (commonly dated c. AD 130–200; the ch. 9 passage is from the main body, not the later chs. 11–12 appendix) — the righteous One bearing the sin of the many so the many are justified. A clean, self-contained atonement passage that names the great exchange without crowning any single atonement theory. New author/work for the corpus; fills the Cross & Salvation bucket. Verified verbatim against source_url (apologia-citations, web, 2026-08-24).
text: O sweet exchange! O unsearchable operation! O benefits surpassing all expectation! That the wickedness of many should be hid in a single righteous One, and that the righteousness of One should justify many transgressors!

author: The Epistle to Diognetus
note: The famous 'soul in the body' image (2nd century) — Christians as the soul of the world, in it but not of it. A clean, iconic Christian Life passage; complements the atonement passage from ch. 9. Verified verbatim against source_url (apologia-citations, web, 2026-08-24).
text: To sum up all in one word—what the soul is in the body, Christians are in the world. The soul is dispersed through all the members of the body, and Christians are scattered through all the cities of the world. The soul dwells in the body, yet is not of the body; and Christians dwell in the world, yet are not of the world.
